problem: exportProviderCatalogSnapshot swallows a failed snapshot write in an empty catch, with no reason given, and then returns { ok: true, path: destPath, summary }. A failed write is reported as success. The function's own doc says it throws so that 'a caller never ships an empty snapshot believing it holds the operator's providers', but here the snapshot is never written at all and the caller still believes it was. `ok` can never be false, so the field tells the caller nothing. This breaks error-handling.mdc Rule 3 / Iron Law 1 (no silent catch before a caller proceeds) and Iron Law 2 (failure must not look like success).
impact: If destPath is unwritable (missing parent dir, read-only volume, EACCES), syncPinnedSnapshot(dir, true) (line 152) returns a success summary and loadOrRefreshWith carries on as if a pinned fallback exists. The operator only learns the pin is missing when an air-gapped start finds no snapshot. Class scope: the only empty catch in the new file; enumerated by reading every catch block in provider-catalog-snapshot.ts (lines 74, 95).

problem: The doc comment on importProviderCatalogSnapshot does not match the code. It says an entry already in the cache that is newer than the snapshot's copy is kept, and only older or missing entries are replaced. The loop (line 129) calls updateProviderCatalogEntry for every accepted entry without comparing fetchedAt, and updateProviderCatalogEntry overwrites unconditionally (provider-catalog-cache.ts:234).
impact: A reader or caller trusts the documented merge rule and imports a pinned snapshot over a fresher live cache. The comment hides that the newer data gets overwritten. The behaviour itself belongs to the logic lens; this finding is the misleading contract.
quote:
An entry already in the cache that is newer than the snapshot's copy
 * is kept; only older or missing entries are replaced.

problem: The provider-count/live-count summary block is copied three times in this diff with only the variable name changed: provider-catalog-snapshot.ts:75-77 (export), provider-catalog-snapshot.ts:139-141 (import), and provider-catalog.ts:363-365 (formatCatalogSummaryLine). formatCatalogSummaryLine already exists for this exact job but the snapshot module re-implements its core.
impact: The definition of 'live' (status === "ok") and the summary wording have to stay in sync by hand at three sites. Changing one, for example counting not-supported as connected, quietly makes the three readouts disagree.
quote:
const liveCount = names.filter((name) => catalog.providers[name]?.status === "ok").length;
  const summary = `${names.length} provider(s), ${liveCount} live`;

problem: syncPinnedSnapshot takes a boolean flag, toPinned, that picks between two opposite operations: export the cache to the pinned file, or import the pinned file into the cache. The two branches share nothing. Call sites read syncPinnedSnapshot(deps.dir, true) / syncPinnedSnapshot(deps.dir, false) (provider-catalog.ts:270, 274). solid-principles.mdc lists a boolean flag that selects between two behaviours as a threshold at any count.
impact: At the call sites in loadOrRefreshWith you cannot tell which direction the copy runs without opening the signature. The two branches also return undefined in different situations (only the import branch can), which the shared signature hides. Two functions, pinCatalogSnapshot / restoreFromPinnedSnapshot, would make both clear.

problem: importProviderCatalogSnapshot (about 57 lines) does two separable jobs at different levels in one function. One is low-level parsing and validation of the snapshot file (read, JSON.parse, object/version/catalog/providers shape checks, sanitize, age filter). The other is cache I/O orchestration (a locked write per entry, a prune pass with a re-read and a locked delete per stale name, then summary formatting). This is I/O mixed with a transform, which solid-principles.mdc reports at any length.
impact: The shape and age rules can only be tested through the real config-dir cache and file locks. Every change to the merge or prune policy means editing the same function that holds the parser. A pure parseProviderCatalogSnapshot(text, now, maxAgeMs) -> { accepted, skipped }, called by a thin I/O shell, would separate the two.

problem: The JSON.parse catch both logs to stderr and rethrows the same error, which error-handling.mdc Rule 5 forbids. The rethrown error is the bare SyntaxError, with no operation or path in its message and no wrapping cause. Every other failure in this function throws `provider catalog snapshot: ... ${srcPath}`, so this one is inconsistent.
impact: A caller that logs the error (as Rule 5 expects) prints it twice, and its own copy does not say which file was bad. A library function also writes straight to process.stderr, which breaks a TUI caller's screen. Wrapping it as throw new Error(`provider catalog snapshot: ${srcPath} is not valid JSON`, { cause: e }) fixes both.
quote:
process.stderr.write(`provider catalog snapshot: ${srcPath} is not valid JSON\n`);
    throw e;

problem: The new pinSnapshot field's doc points readers to `keryx providers pin`, but no such command exists. A search of src for 'providers pin' finds only this comment, and nothing in src sets pinSnapshot. The comment documents an entry point that does not exist. The same applies to formatCatalogSummaryLine's 'One line for `keryx providers status`' (line 361): the function has no caller in src.
impact: A maintainer who follows the pointer to find how pinning is turned on finds nothing, and may conclude the feature ships when it is unreachable. Either wire the command and the status line, or describe what the code actually provides.
quote: /** Keep a pinned copy of every saved catalog, and fall back to it when a refresh finds nothing (`keryx providers pin`). */

problem: In syncPinnedSnapshot's import branch, readConfigFile is used only as an existence probe, then the result is thrown away and importProviderCatalogSnapshot reads the same file again. pinnedSnapshotFile(dir) is also computed three times in this function.
impact: There is a small duplicate read and a check-then-use split. A file removed between the two reads produces a throw instead of the undefined the probe was meant to give. Resolving the path once and branching on a single read is clearer.
quote:
const pinned = readConfigFile(pinnedSnapshotFile(dir));
  if (!pinned.ok) return undefined;
